{"rules": ["Model consistently underestimates volatility and fails to capture sharp upward spikes (e.g., +3-5 EUR) that occur after a period of low sentiment or consolidation.", "Forecast shows excessive mean reversion bias, predicting a slow linear decline when true outcomes exhibit high-frequency oscillations around the current level.", "When recent history ends with a price spike followed by neutral sentiment, the model fails to sustain the upward momentum, resulting in an early peak and subsequent under-forecast of the new high.", "Model ignores the 'momentum lag' effect where sentiment spikes (0.40) precede price action; forecasts should be adjusted upward if sentiment is rising even if recent prices are flat.", "In volatile regimes (price range 78-95 EUR), model drifts downward too quickly, failing to account for mean-reversion bounces that push prices above the linear projection.", "Apply a volatility correction factor: increase forecast variance by ~10-15% during periods where sentiment history shows alternating 0.20/0.40 signals despite flat recent prices."]
